name: niubash-release-preinstall
description: Release CI pre-install manifest (niubash#189, extended by niubash#209). The release workflow installs every entry of `packages` into the staged WinuxCmd root with `winuxcmd wpm install <name> --root <staged-root> --yes`, then materializes every entry of `shims` as a winuxcmd.exe hardlink in usr\bin. The package index lives in unixwin/wpm-source (index.json); wpm itself ships inside winuxcmd.exe (`winuxcmd wpm ...`), so no separate wpm.exe is needed.

packages.name: gawk
packages.purpose: GNU Awk 5.4.1. bash-it plugins and completions hard-depend on awk (the gradle completion pipes through `awk '{print $1}'` on every use); gawk IS the GNU implementation, so plugin scripts written against GNU awk keep their dialect. The wpm `gawk` package is layout=shim: the payload (gawk.exe, awk.exe, and its five DLLs) lands in <root>\opt\gawk and usr\bin\gawk.exe is a winuxcmd.exe hardlink shim that forwards there.

packages.name: niugit
packages.purpose: Niu-git 2.55.0.3 (native Windows git without MSYS). The full plugin distro (oh-my-bash, omb-theme-robbyrussell, bash-it, bash-completion, bash-preexec) installs every entry through git clone/pull, so a fresh machine without git.exe on PATH failed all five with 'failed to run git; is git.exe on PATH?' (niubash#209). Bundling niugit removes the hard dependency on the user's environment. The payload is the whole niu-git tree (git.exe at the package root plus the mingw64/ directory carrying its minimal dependency DLLs and etc/) landing in <root>\opt\niugit; wpm registers command `git`, so usr\bin\git.exe forwards into the package. It is schannel-only TLS with no bundled shell/perl and accepts POSIX-shaped (/d/...) path args.

packages.name: ripgrep
packages.purpose: Ripgrep 15.2.0 (`rg`). A common interactive/search tool users expect right after first setup; shipped so the out-of-the-box shell has modern search without a network fetch (niubash#209). Single static rg.exe payload in <root>\opt\ripgrep with command `rg` registered. Unlike niugit/gawk, the wpm index carries a windows-arm64 artifact too, so this one pre-installs on BOTH Windows legs.

packages.name: fd
packages.purpose: fd 10.4.2. The find counterpart to ripgrep; same rationale (niubash#209): bundled at CI time so users never need a network install for the basics. Single static fd.exe payload in <root>\opt\fd with command `fd` registered, with a windows-arm64 artifact in the index as well.

shims.name: awk
shims.reason: bash-it calls plain `awk`, not `gawk`. The wpm gawk package only registers `commands: [gawk]`, so wpm alone leaves usr\bin without an awk.exe and winuxcmd has no awk builtin to catch the name. The release step hardlinks usr\bin\awk.exe to usr\bin\winuxcmd.exe (exactly what wpm's create_package_shims does); the shim dispatcher then forwards `awk` to opt\gawk\awk.exe from the package payload. This mirrors how MSYS presents gawk as awk.

notes: Fail-open contract: a failed install is a loud warning (GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY + ::warning), never a release blocker. Pre-installing is an enhancement, not a promise; users can always run `winuxcmd wpm install <name>` against an installed package.

Architecture: niugit and gawk exist as windows-x64 artifacts only in the wpm index; on the arm64 release leg those installs fail by design and the leg ships without them. ripgrep and fd carry windows-arm64 artifacts and pre-install on both legs. The post-package verify step asserts only on legs where the binaries exist.

No symlinks, ever: shims are winuxcmd.exe hardlinks (copies on file systems without hardlink support). The issue red lines stand - no archive formats are added, no symbolic links are created, and the runtime never downloads binaries (the assembly happens here, in CI).
The staged package ships <root>\usr\bin shims and the <root>\opt payload tree only - never the .wpm state directory (cache/staging/index).

excluded.name: goawk
excluded.reason: Owner decision (gawk only): goawk is forbidden in the pre-install manifest. Plugins target GNU awk; a second awk dialect on PATH is a compatibility hazard, not an enhancement. (The separate wpm `awk` package is likewise not installed: it is the same upstream artifact as `gawk` — gawk-5.4.1, same SHA-256 — and the awk command is provided by the shims entry above.)

excluded.name: bzip2
excluded.reason: Owner decision: no compression tools in the pre-install manifest. Users install bzip2 themselves via `winuxcmd wpm install bzip2` when they need it.

excluded.name: gzip
excluded.reason: Owner decision: no compression tools in the pre-install manifest. Users install gzip themselves via `winuxcmd wpm install gzip` when they need it.

excluded.name: link
excluded.reason: Owner directive: FORBIDDEN FOREVER. The name collides with the MSVC link.exe toolchain binary; it must never appear in packages or shims of any manifest revision.
